title: From Folk Medicine to Therapeutic Innovation: An Updated Review of the Ethnomedicinal Uses, Bioactive Constituents, and Antidiabetic and Anti-Infective Potential of Uvaria chamae P. Beauv. (Annonaceae)
content: Uvaria chamae, commonly known as finger root or bush banana, has attracted considerable interest across West Africa due to its ethnomedicinal importance, edible value, and reported antidiabetic and anti-infectious properties. Thus, increasing demand for the species in traditional medicine has led to intensive harvesting from the wild, threatening its survival. Despite its significance, knowledge essential for its sustainable management, conservation, and utilization remains limited and fragmented. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to-date synthesis of the existing knowledge on U. chamae. Relevant literature was retrieved through systematic searches across PubMed, Scopus, Embase, ResearchGate, African Journals Online, and the Environmental Science Collection using structured and targeted search terms. The review covers taxonomy, geographical distribution, ecology, morphological variation, propagation techniques, phytochemical composition, and documented health benefits of the species. In addition, it critically evaluates current evidence regarding its antidiabetic and anti-infectious activities, toxicity profile, and potential clinical applications. The available evidence highlights U. chamae as a promising source of bioactive compounds with potential for the development of antidiabetic and anti-infectious therapeutics. By consolidating current knowledge and identifying existing research gaps, this review provides a foundation for future studies and supports ongoing efforts toward conservation, domestication, sustainable utilization, and valorization of U. chamae.
